answer: Cryptographic proof-of-work protocols restrict autonomous AI agent Sybil attacks by tying node identity generation to verifiable computational expenditure. Each participating agent must periodically solve a hard cryptographic puzzle broadcasted by a network beacon. Because compute resources cannot be infinitely scaled without proportional capital, forging a massive island of fake nodes becomes economically prohibitive. Consequently, the resulting economic plume of energy consumption defends the decentralized consensus state against unauthorized takeover attempts by malicious actors.
